# CLAUDE.md — docs/teaching/ (the student handouts)

**Purpose:** Print-ready handouts that explain a trading model to a human — Aaron's community and
his students. **Nothing here is read by any code.**
**Scope:** The HTML sources, their rendered PDFs, and the diagram assets. Does NOT cover the specs
those handouts are derived from (`docs/DAVINCI_MODEL_SPEC.md`), the source notes
(`education/learned/`), or the scanner that measures the model (`backtest/tools/loaded_level_scan.py`
— see `backtest/CLAUDE.md`).
**Status:** Three handouts, all hand-rendered, none generated by a build step.

---

## The rule that matters here

🔴 **A handout is a CLAIM about a model, and it will be read by people who cannot check it.** That
is the opposite of every other document in this repo, where the reader can open the code. So:

- **Every number in a handout names where it came from, or it does not go in.** Root rule 4 with
  higher stakes — a guessed figure in a spec sends the next engineer to a one-command check, a
  guessed figure in a handout gets traded.
- **A measured result and a teaching illustration are labelled differently.** The schematic charts
  in `marco_vs_yours.svg` are DRAWN, not replayed, and the artwork says so in its own footer. Keep
  that footer.
- **Where the source material and Aaron's own practice DISAGREE, say so on the page** rather than
  smoothing it over. `Marco_vs_Yours.pdf` exists because they disagree about entry timing, and
  flattening that into one "correct" method would be the whole error.

## What is here

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `three_models.html` / `Three_Trading_Models.pdf` | Sequence reference for three liquidity models, at summary level. Model 3 is the Loaded Level model the other two files expand. |
| `loaded_level_model.html` / `Loaded_Level_Model.pdf` | 8-page beginner handout for the Loaded Level model — written for first exposure, no prior SMC vocabulary assumed. Three inline SVG diagrams. |
| `rso_and_els.svg` / `.png` | The two strategies this repo is actually building, side by side: **RSO — Retail Shake Out** (`docs/MPC_FB_SPEC.md`) and **ELS — Engineered Liquidity Sweep** (`docs/DAVINCI_MODEL_SPEC.md`). Schematic candles plus a checklist per strategy, each row naming the engine field behind it. The SVG is the editable master. |
| `marco_vs_yours.svg` / `.png` / `Marco_vs_Yours.pdf` | 4-page comparison of the source author's entry (on the sweep) against Aaron's (on the pullback into the gap between two lower highs). Same arming event, different fill. Generated once by hand; the SVG is the editable master. |

## How a PDF gets made

There is **no build step and no pandoc/weasyprint/wkhtmltopdf on this machine** — all three were
checked and are absent. Chrome headless renders the print CSS:

```bash
"/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome" --headless --disable-gpu \
  --no-pdf-header-footer --print-to-pdf="docs/teaching/<Name>.pdf" \
  "file://$PWD/docs/teaching/<name>.html"
```

⚠ **Verify a re-render by LOOKING at it, never by grepping the PDF for text.** Chrome subsets the
embedded fonts, so a `grep` for a string you just added returns zero on a perfectly correct file —
that was tried, it read as a failed render, and it was not one. Screenshot the page and read the
image.

⚠ **SVG labels overlap in ways the markup does not reveal.** Three collisions shipped in the first
Loaded Level render (text over a price line, a caption clipping a path, a label under the entry
dot) and none was visible without rendering. Render to PNG and read it before calling a diagram
done.

## The naming, and why it is not cosmetic

Two strategies, two fixed names. They are used in the handouts, the specs and the code, and they
do **not** carry the name of whoever taught them.

| Name | Code | Spec |
|---|---|---|
| **RSO — Retail Shake Out** | `mpc_fb` | `docs/MPC_FB_SPEC.md` |
| **ELS — Engineered Liquidity Sweep** | `mpc_els` | `docs/DAVINCI_MODEL_SPEC.md` |

🔴 **"Shakeout" now means exactly one thing in this repo, and getting there cost a deletion.**
`mpc_d_strategy.pine` used the word for a different setup entirely — its middle leg, with an input
literally documented as "how much the shakeout may break before it stops being a shakeout". Two
setups sharing one term is how a rule gets read backwards, so D was removed on 2026-08-15 (see
`indicators/strategies/CLAUDE.md`). **Do not reintroduce the word for anything but RSO.**

⚠ **Aaron's own pullback entry is an ELS ENTRY MODE, not a third strategy.** He waits for
RSO-style confirmation but takes an ELS level. Building it as a separate package would give one
setup two names, which is the mistake above from the other direction.

## Rules

- **Never publish a handout for a model whose measurement contradicts it without saying so.** The
  Loaded Level handout carries a "what we actually measured" page for this reason, including the
  side that did NOT beat its control.
- **Keep the artwork's master format editable.** `marco_vs_yours.svg` is the source; the PNG and PDF
  are derived. Do not hand-edit the derived files.
- **These files are committed.** They are the deliverable, not scratch output.
